candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is a systemic vasculitis, Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis. Lumbosacral plexopathy is a localized nerve disorder, not a systemic condition.
Common peroneal nerve palsy (foot drop) is a manifestation of the peripheral neuropathy associated with Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis, not the underlying systemic disease itself.
Lumbar disc herniation was an initial diagnosis but the patient's condition progressed to a systemic vasculitis (EGPA) which is the reference diagnosis. These are distinct entities.

Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) is a distinct autoimmune neuropathy. While EGPA can cause neuropathy, it is a systemic vasculitis with specific diagnostic criteria that differentiate it from CIDP.

This candidate translates to 'Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) with peripheral neuropathy (right foot drop)', which is a complete and accurate description of the reference diagnosis and its key manifestation in this case.
